mcqs.learning_point: Represent solutions on a number line
mcqs.question: The inequality 3x - 5 \le 7 simplifies to x \le 4. Which of the following number‑line diagrams correctly represents the solution set?

options.A: A closed circle at 4 with a solid arrow pointing to the left (including all numbers less than or equal to 4).
options.B: An open circle at 4 with a solid arrow pointing to the left (excluding 4).
options.C: A closed circle at 4 with a solid arrow pointing to the right (including numbers greater than or equal to 4).
options.D: An open circle at 4 with a solid arrow pointing to the right (excluding 4).

mcqs.answer: A closed circle at 4 with a solid arrow pointing to the left (including all numbers less than or equal to 4).
mcqs.explanation: Since the solution is x \le 4, the point 4 must be included (closed circle) and the arrow must extend toward smaller numbers (left). Option A shows exactly this. Option B excludes 4, which is wrong. Options C and D point to the opposite direction, representing x \ge 4, which does not match the inequality.

mcqs.question: Express the solution set of the inequality -3 < x \le 5 in interval notation.
mcqs.explanation: The inequality -3 < x means x is greater than -3 but not equal, so the left endpoint is an open parenthesis. x \le 5 includes 5, so the right endpoint is a closed bracket. Hence the correct interval notation is (-3,5]. Options B and D use a closed bracket at -3, which would include -3, and option C excludes 5, both incorrect.

mcqs.question: Consider the compound inequalities (i) 2 < x < 6 and (ii) x \le 5. Which statement about their solution sets is true?

options.A: The solution set of (i) is a subset of the solution set of (ii).
options.B: The solution set of (ii) is a subset of the solution set of (i).
options.C: Both have exactly the same solution set.

mcqs.answer: The solution set of (i) is a subset of the solution set of (ii).
mcqs.explanation: Inequality (i) gives 2 < x < 6, i.e., all numbers between 2 and 6, not including the endpoints. Inequality (ii) gives x \le 5, i.e., all numbers up to and including 5. Every number satisfying (i) also satisfies (ii) because any x between 2 and 5 is allowed, and the part (5,6) of (i) does not satisfy (ii). Thus the set of (i) is contained within the set of (ii). Option A states this correctly. Options B, C, and D are false.

mcqs.question: If the solution set of a linear inequality in one variable is (-\infty, -2) \cup (3, \infty), which of the following inequalities represents it?
mcqs.explanation: The interval (-\infty, -2) corresponds to all numbers less than -2 (strict inequality), and (3, \infty) corresponds to all numbers greater than 3 (strict inequality). Therefore the combined solution is "x < -2 or x > 3", which is option A. Option B uses "\le" and "\ge", which would include -2 and 3, contradicting the open intervals. Options C and D describe the intersection of the two intervals, which would be the empty set, not the given union.
